findings.title: ISR requests expose the internal path as a query parameter
findings.why_it_matters: Pages and middleware see x_astro_path in Astro.url and Request.url even when the visitor supplied no query string. Applications that branch on query presence, preserve a return URL, or generate canonical URLs consequently produce incorrect output for ISR requests.
evidence: packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts:63 rewrites every ISR route to /_isr?x_astro_path=$0, and the prerender configuration at line 713 sets passQuery: true.

The new branch reads x_astro_path from url.searchParams at line 25, but only changes pathname before constructing the Request at line 29; the internal parameter remains in the URL passed to app.render.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the adapter-owned x_astro_path query parameter after recovering the path, before constructing the Request, while preserving other query parameters.

residual_risks: Vercel platform behavior, including whether its ISR header is always present and how it encodes substituted paths, could not be verified in this environment.
